title: Anthropic IPO breaks all records, even SpaceX! What $81.3 billion means for India's IT and AI stocks? Experts decode | Stock Market News
text:
The artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom has reached a new milestone, with Anthropic raising a record $81.3 billion through its initial public offering (IPO), surpassing Elon Musk's SpaceX and putting the spotlight firmly on the global AI industry. Anthropic's record-breaking IPO raises questions about how the growing dominance of AI model developers could reshape India's IT and technology stocks.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, said on Thursday, November 19, that it had upsized its IPO, selling 980 million shares against the 825 million planned earlier. The company priced the shares at $83 apiece, above its initial range of $70–78. Underwriters have also been given a 30-day option to purchase an additional 147 million shares. The stock is scheduled to list on Nasdaq.

The IPO has already raised $81.3 billion, exceeding the $75 billion raised by SpaceX earlier this year. SpaceX's total fundraising subsequently reached $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment option. Anthropic's fundraising could cross $100 billion when investments worth $26 billion from technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD, are taken into account.

The deal values Anthropic at around $1.5 trillion, underscoring the premium investors are willing to pay for companies developing foundational AI models and enterprise AI platforms.

For India's IT sector, the development presents both an opportunity and a challenge. Rising global AI spending could create fresh demand for cloud modernisation, AI integration, data engineering, cybersecurity and enterprise transformation. However, automation could also disrupt traditional IT services, putting pressure on pricing and employee-based billing models.

Mohit Gulati, Managing Partner at ITI Alternatives, said Anthropic's ability to raise more than SpaceX reflects where global capital expects value to be created over the next decade — in companies that own the intelligence layer.

For Indian IT companies, he said, this should serve as a wake-up call rather than a death sentence. While the country's largest IT firms have strong client relationships and enterprise implementation capabilities, they need to reposition themselves from selling employee hours to delivering AI-led business outcomes.

Viram Shah, Founder and CEO of Vested, said Anthropic's IPO highlights investor appetite for AI businesses, but its implications for Indian IT companies are more nuanced. While Anthropic develops AI technology, Indian IT firms largely focus on its implementation and integration.

He cautioned that AI adoption could create significant opportunities while also disrupting traditional services. Companies that convert AI adoption into measurable client outcomes and revenue growth are likely to benefit the most.

Shah also stressed that Anthropic's valuation does not automatically justify a re-rating of Indian IT stocks. Their valuations will depend on how effectively they adopt AI and develop commercially viable use cases.

Saurabh Jain, Head of Fundamental Research at SMC Global Securities, said Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO underscores strong investor appetite for artificial intelligence (AI) and validates the technology’s long-term growth potential.

For Indian IT companies, the development presents an opportunity as accelerating AI adoption could drive demand for AI integration, cloud computing, data analytics and digital transformation services. However, it also raises concerns over automation, pricing pressure and disruption to traditional outsourcing models.

Jain said the key differentiator for Indian IT companies would be their ability to monetise AI through higher-value services rather than merely adopting the technology. Companies with strong AI capabilities, strategic partnerships and clear revenue visibility from AI-led solutions are likely to emerge as long-term winners.

Among large-cap IT companies, TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Wipro are worth watching because of their enterprise relationships and ability to deploy AI solutions at scale. Shah also pointed to opportunities in specialised companies focused on engineering, cloud modernisation, data infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Gaurav Garg, Head – Research at Lemonn, said Indian IT companies could benefit from increased global spending on AI integration, cloud infrastructure, data engineering and automation. However, he cautioned that AI tools could automate coding, testing and routine maintenance, potentially reducing demand for conventional IT services and putting pressure on margins.

Garg said investors should focus on companies with established enterprise relationships, strong AI capabilities, healthy order pipelines and the ability to translate AI investments into earnings. He favoured a selective approach rather than a broad-based bullish view on IT stocks.

Within the sector, investors can track large-cap names such as TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Wipro, alongside mid-cap technology companies including Persistent Systems, Coforge, LTIMindtree and Mphasis. Companies with exposure to data centres, AI infrastructure and cloud computing, such as Netweb Technologies and E2E Networks, also remain on the radar, although their business exposure differs from that of IT services providers.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said the record IPO demonstrates that global capital is flowing towards AI model developers, chipmakers and infrastructure companies, rather than directly towards IT services firms.

He said the central question for Indian IT companies is whether new opportunities in data, cloud migration and integration will be sufficient to offset pricing pressure and the automation of legacy services. Investors should monitor AI-related revenue, deal wins and margins over the coming quarters rather than react solely to headline IPO valuations.
